items.stem: Why can a material behave very differently at the nanoscale than in bulk form?

options.text: At the nanoscale, a large fraction of atoms are at the surface and quantum effects can dominate, changing properties
options.rationale: Correct: high surface-to-volume ratio and quantum effects alter optical, chemical and electronic behaviour.

options.text: Because nanoscale materials are simply lighter versions of the bulk
options.rationale: The change is qualitative (new properties), not just lighter.

options.text: Because measuring tools make up the differences
options.rationale: The differences are real physical effects, not measurement artefacts.

options.text: Because nanoscale materials contain different chemical elements by definition
options.rationale: Same element can show new behaviour at the nanoscale without changing composition.

items.explanation: Correct: high surface-to-volume ratio and quantum effects alter optical, chemical and electronic behaviour.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about nanotechnology fabrication are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Top-down approaches carve or pattern structures from larger material
options.rationale: Correct: top-down methods start big and remove/pattern down to nanoscale.

options.text: Bottom-up approaches build structures by assembling atoms or molecules
options.rationale: Correct: bottom-up methods grow or self-assemble nanostructures from components.

options.text: Self-assembly requires no control over conditions
options.rationale: Self-assembly depends on carefully controlled chemistry and conditions.

options.text: Top-down and bottom-up are the same process
options.rationale: They are distinct, complementary fabrication strategies.

items.explanation: Correct: top-down methods start big and remove/pattern down to nanoscale.

items.stem: Why is nanosafety a legitimate consideration for products containing engineered nanoparticles?

options.text: Their small size and novel properties can lead to biological and environmental behaviour not seen in the bulk material
options.rationale: Correct: nanoparticles may interact with cells and ecosystems differently, warranting careful assessment.

options.text: Because nanoparticles are always more toxic than any other substance
options.rationale: Toxicity varies; the point is novel behaviour needing assessment, not blanket toxicity.

options.text: Because nanoparticles cannot be measured so risk is unknowable
options.rationale: They can be characterised; risk assessment is possible, if careful.

options.text: Because safety never differs from the bulk material
options.rationale: Nanoscale behaviour can differ from bulk, which is exactly why safety is considered.

items.explanation: Correct: nanoparticles may interact with cells and ecosystems differently, warranting careful assessment.
